ART_19_1_D.title: Freedom of Movement
ART_19_1_D.explanation: All citizens have the right to move freely throughout the territory of India. This means you have the right to travel, walk, and move in public spaces without unreasonable restriction.
key_points: Police cannot restrict without legal grounds
what_you_can_ask: Under which law are you stopping me?
Do you have a warrant or court order?
What is the legal basis for this restriction?
Am I free to leave?
ART_19_1_D.punishment_if_violated: Not criminal, but police action may be challenged in court as unconstitutional
references: Supreme Court: Malik v. State AIR 1954

ART_21.title: Protection of Life and Personal Liberty
ART_21.explanation: No person shall be deprived of their life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. This is a fundamental right protecting dignity, freedom, and bodily integrity.
what_you_can_ask: Why am I being detained?
Do you have authority to search me?
What is the legal procedure being followed?
I want to speak to a lawyer
ART_21.punishment_if_violated: May be challenged as violation of fundamental right; compensation possible
references: Supreme Court: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India

IPC_341.title: Wrongful Restraint
IPC_341.explanation: Wrongful restraint is when a person prevents another from moving in any direction without legal authority. This includes blocking movement, holding, or detaining without lawful reason.
key_points: Applies when restraint has no legal basis
Police must have warrant or reasonable suspicion
Consent matters – agreed stop is not restraint
what_you_can_ask: On what suspicion are you restraining me?
Do you have a warrant?
Am I free to leave?
What law are you invoking?
IPC_341.punishment_if_violated: Up to 1 month imprisonment or Rs 250 fine or both
references: Supreme Court: Sube Singh v. State of Punjab AIR 1989

IPC_342.title: Wrongful Confinement
IPC_342.explanation: Wrongful confinement is wrongful restraint in an enclosed space (like a room, vehicle, station) that prevents escape. It's a more serious form of unlawful detention.
key_points: Requires deliberate confinement without legal basis
what_you_can_ask: On what authority am I being confined?
What is the legal procedure?
Can I contact my family or lawyer?
How long will I be held?
IPC_342.punishment_if_violated: Up to 3 months imprisonment or Rs 500 fine or both
references: Supreme Court: Lalita Kumari v. Government of UP

IPC_354.title: Assault or Criminal Force to Woman with Intent to Outrage Modesty
IPC_354.explanation: Using force or threatening to use force against a woman with intent to outrage modesty. Includes unwanted touching, pulling, grabbing that violates dignity or modesty.
key_points: Applies to any unwanted touching that violates modesty
Can be committed by anyone, including police
Victim's perception of violation is important
what_you_can_ask: Do you have authority for body search?
Why are you touching me?
I don't consent to this search
This violates my dignity and modesty
IPC_354.punishment_if_violated: Up to 3 years imprisonment and/or Rs 2000 fine; if by public servant: up to 2 years more
references: Supreme Court: Sakshi v. Union of India AIR 2004

IPC_504.title: Intentional Insult with Knowledge of Causing Breach of Peace
IPC_504.explanation: Uttering words or making gestures with intent to insult or knowing it will provoke breach of peace. Includes disrespect, abusive language, humiliation.
key_points: Must have intent or knowledge of provocation
what_you_can_ask: I am being insulted and humiliated
This language is disrespectful
I want your name and badge number
I will file a complaint
IPC_504.punishment_if_violated: Up to 3 months imprisonment or Rs 250 fine or both
references: Supreme Court: Sharma v. State AIR 1995

IPC_506.title: Criminal Intimidation
IPC_506.explanation: Making threats of injury to person, property, reputation with intent to cause fear or to compel a person to do something. Includes threats of arrest, violence, harm.
key_points: Threat must be credible and serious
Intent to cause fear or coerce is required
Includes threats of arrest without cause
what_you_can_ask: That is a threat. I don't appreciate it
I will record this threat
I want your name and badge number
I will file a complaint for intimidation
IPC_506.punishment_if_violated: Up to 2 years imprisonment or Rs 1000 fine or both; 7 years if threat is by letter/object
references: Supreme Court: Pradeep Kumar v. State of Bihar

IPC_509.title: Word, Gesture, Act Intended to Insult Modesty of Woman
IPC_509.explanation: Using words, gestures, or acts to insult modesty of a woman. Includes unwanted attention, leering, offensive questions about personal life.
key_points: Applies to conduct that violates modesty
what_you_can_ask: That question is inappropriate and violates my modesty
My personal relationships are not your concern
This is harassment
I want to file a complaint
IPC_509.punishment_if_violated: Up to 3 months imprisonment or Rs 200 fine or both
references: Supreme Court: Vishakha v. State of Rajasthan

IPC_420.title: Cheating
IPC_420.explanation: Cheating is deceiving a person to induce them to deliver property or risk it. Includes fraud, false promises, deceptive practices for personal gain.
key_points: Person must suffer loss or risk of loss
what_you_can_ask: I want to file complaint for cheating
Can you help me recover my money?
What evidence do I need?
How long does investigation take?
IPC_420.punishment_if_violated: Up to 7 years imprisonment and/or fine up to Rs 1000
references: Supreme Court: Ajay Mandal v. State of Maharashtra

CRPC_41.title: When Police Can Arrest Without Warrant
CRPC_41.explanation: Police can arrest without warrant only in specific circumstances: serious offense, flight risk, evidence tampering, or obstruction of justice. Mere suspicion is not enough.
key_points: Police need warrant for most arrests
Without warrant: only for serious crimes
Police must give reason for arrest
You have right to know charges
what_you_can_ask: On what charge are you arresting me?
Where is your warrant?
What is the legal basis for this arrest?
I want to call a lawyer
CRPC_41.punishment_if_violated: Illegal arrest can be challenged; person may claim damages
references: Supreme Court: Joginder Kumar v. State of UP AIR 1994

CRPC_50.title: Person Arrested to be Informed of Grounds of Arrest and Right to Legal Counsel
CRPC_50.explanation: When arrested, you must be informed of: (1) the grounds of arrest, (2) right to legal counsel, (3) right to inform a relative. This is a fundamental procedural right.
key_points: Must be told why you are arrested
what_you_can_ask: Tell me why I am being arrested
I want to call my family
I want to contact a lawyer
Write down these rights for me
CRPC_50.punishment_if_violated: Arrest may be illegal; evidence can be inadmissible
references: Supreme Court: Janak Raj v. State AIR 1983

CRPC_160.title: Examination of Accused by Police Officer
CRPC_160.explanation: Police can question a person for investigation. However: you can refuse and must be told reason; questions at police station only with permission; lawyer can be present.
key_points: You can ask why you're being questioned
You have right to refuse initially
Right to have lawyer present during formal questioning
what_you_can_ask: Why do you want to question me?
Am I under arrest or can I leave?
Can my lawyer be present?
What questions do you want to ask?
CRPC_160.punishment_if_violated: Confessions obtained illegally may be inadmissible in court
references: Supreme Court: Khatri v. State of Bihar

CRPC_165.title: Police Search Without Warrant (Limited Circumstances)
CRPC_165.explanation: Police can search person/property only: with warrant, with consent, or in limited emergency situations. Body search requires special procedure and female officer.
key_points: Consent must be voluntary and written if possible
Female officer must conduct female body search
No degrading or indecent search allowed
what_you_can_ask: Do you have a search warrant?
On what legal grounds are you searching?
I do not consent to this search
A female officer must conduct any body search
CRPC_165.punishment_if_violated: Illegal search evidence inadmissible; compensation possible
references: Supreme Court: Shamla Devi v. State

IT_ACT_66.title: Computer Hacking
IT_ACT_66.explanation: Accessing computer system/network without authorization, or exceeding authorized access. Includes hacking accounts, stealing data, unauthorized entry.
key_points: Can apply to both criminal and civil cases
what_you_can_ask: My account was hacked. How do I file complaint?
What do I need to prove hacking?
Can evidence be recovered?
What are the criminal penalties?
IT_ACT_66.punishment_if_violated: Up to 3 years imprisonment and/or fine up to Rs 5 lakh
references: Supreme Court: Pushpendra Singh Chauhan v. State

IT_ACT_66D.title: Cheating by Personation Using Computer Resource
IT_ACT_66D.explanation: Using computer to cheat by impersonating someone, creating fake profiles, or deceiving for money/property. Includes online fraud, fake identities, phishing scams.
what_you_can_ask: Someone created a fake profile in my name
I lost money to an online scam
What evidence do I need to prove fraud?
How long does investigation take?
IT_ACT_66D.punishment_if_violated: Up to 3 years imprisonment and/or fine up to Rs 1 lakh
references: Supreme Court cases on cyber fraud

JJ_ACT.section: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
JJ_ACT.title: Protection of Minors During Police Custody
JJ_ACT.explanation: Children (under 18) have special protections: police must inform parents immediately, no third-degree, specialized procedures, presence of guardian during questioning.
key_points: Applies to all persons under 18 years
Child cannot be detained for long without parents
what_you_can_ask: My child is detained. Where is my child?
Who authorized this detention?
Can I take my child home?
Can I be present during questioning?
JJ_ACT.punishment_if_violated: Police action illegal; child must be released immediately; compensation possible
